summary: Curry County, OR ground lookout in the Siskiyou NF: L-5 cab from 1933, steel cab from 1955 or 1957, moved by helicopter in 1973/74; concrete blocks remain.

facts.design: L-5 cab (1933), later replaced by a steel cab (1955 per most sources; 1957 per Oregon Lookouts)
facts.status_note: The steel cab was flown by helicopter to Lake of the Woods Lookout in 1973 or 1974; only some concrete blocks and guy cable anchors remain at the site per Oregon Hikers

staffing.status: seasonal lookout; 65 days in 1941; newspaper items name lookouts in 1967 and 1972

access.note: Barklow Mountain Trail #1258 in the Copper Salmon Wilderness; year-round use; wilderness regulations apply, no motorized or mechanized use

visit.trail_note: Trail #1258 follows the ridge to the old lookout site from the northeast trailhead, reached by about five miles on Forest Road 3353

events.note: New lookout packed to the mountain in August 1933; L-5 cab per the Register, Firelookout.com and Oregon Hikers
Staffed 65 days, reporting to the Powers Ranger Station by West Coast Telephone
Steel cab replaced the L-5 cab per the Register, Firelookout.com and Oregon Hikers; Oregon Lookouts dates a new all-steel house to 1957
Newspaper item reprinted by Oregon Lookouts names a lookout on Barklow Mountain
Newspaper item reprinted by Oregon Lookouts says a couple went up to the Barklow lookout
Cab moved to Lake of the Woods Lookout; Oregon Hikers and Oregon Lookouts say by helicopter; Oregon Lookouts dates the flight to 1973

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register, Firelookout.com and Oregon Hikers give 1955 for the steel cab; Oregon Lookouts dates a new all-steel house to 1957. The story reports both.
The Register, Firelookout.com and Oregon Hikers say the cab moved in 1974; Oregon Lookouts says the flight was in 1973. The story reports both.

The 1942 survey describes a 10-by-10-foot building about 10 feet high; Oregon Lookouts gives 13 by 13 feet for the 1957 steel house. These describe different buildings, so height_m 3.0 refers to the 1942 description.

notes_for_editor: Height 3.0 m in the record matches the 1942 survey's about-10-feet description, which may be of an earlier building than the 1957 steel house. Design is sourced from the 1933 L-5 entry; no design is in the brief. Replacement year (1955 vs 1957) and move year (1973 vs 1974) disagree and are both reported. The 1967 and 1972 staffing items come from newspaper clippings reprinted on Oregon Lookouts and were not checked against the papers. No photos added: the Register's panorama photo credits had no image URLs in the pages read. The Forest Service trail page was last updated August 12, 2025. Fact-check 2026-10-09: the helicopter move is attributed only to Oregon Hikers and Oregon Lookouts, not the Register or Firelookout.com.
